description.narrative: The Program will be financed through a PforR component and IPF component. The following activities will be financed under the IPF: (a) Electronic Digital Signature (EDS) application system based on SIM cards integrated into ITMIS; (b) Electronic registration and accounting system for cash registers; (c) Electronic labeling of goods; (d) Electronic counter; (e) Tax monitoring system for the subjects of taxation; (f) Analytical system based on BigData analysis; (g) Module of end-to-end monitoring of business entities in the gambling business; (h) System for registration and tax accounting of e-commerce entities; (i) Module of self-service for self-employed subjects and households ; (j) Module of tax accounting for transactions in the real estate market; (k) Automated VAT refund system; (l) Training module for continuous training and improving employee knowledge; (m) Training module for taxpayers; (n) Education platform for university students; (o) Electronic income statement for individuals; (p) Electronic confirmation of financial balance for legal entities; (q) Electronic applications for confirmation tax benefits; (r) Legal assistant for registration of small businesses; (s) Tariffication module; (t) Multilingual electronic tax code; (u) Development of a discussion platform for taxpayers; (v) Tax burden calculator; (w) Development of an adjusted API for the purpose of integrating electronic services; (x) Accounting system for small and medium businesses; (y) Integration modules with statistics and pension fund for cross-verification of data; (z) E- assistant for taxpayers; (aa) Development of a module for tax accounting and analysis based on artificial intelligence (AI); (bb) Module for integration of payments for tax and other tax services with existing and alternative payment systems; (cc) Development and implementation of "Taxpayer" - an interactive electronic application for mobile devices for Android and IOS platforms; (dd) Electronic residency confirmation; (ee) Development of MoF information and analytical system for automation of state revenue accounting, analysis and forecasting and (ff) A module for taxpayer feedback mechanism at the Contact Center. The IPF component of the operation will also finance support to overall Program implementation and management, including the maintenance of a Program Implementation Group (PIG) with adequate implementation and fiduciary capacity, and support for verification of DLIs according to established protocols. The PIG team will comprise local consultants to ensure financial management, disbursement and adherence to the relevant procurement rules as will be stipulated in the Loan Agreement and the Project Operational Manual. In addition, the PIG will hire M&E consultants, who will be responsible for monitoring of the progress on achieving the Project results and preparation of the progress reports under the Project. The component will finance services of the audit firm, which will be hired to verify the results under DLIs according to the established protocols. The PIG will also hire Social and Environmental Specialists to ensure fulfillment of the environmental and social safeguards responsibilities under the Program and IT Consultants to support procurement activities under the Program.
To simplify the tax system, enhance quality of taxpayer services, and improve voluntary compliance.

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.2. The Recipient shall maintain, throughout the Operation implementation: (i) thedeputy chairman of TC as the Operation director; and (ii) the tax administration related activities to be led by the deputychairman of the TC, and tax policy related activities to be led by the deputy minister of finance.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.3. The Recipient, through the TC, shall establish not later than two (2) months fromthe Effective Date and thereafter maintain, throughout the Operation implementation, a Program implementation group (“PIG”)responsible for the monitoring of the Operation, with composition, functions, staffing, facilities and other resources satisfactoryto the Association and as described in the Operational Manual.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.4. The Recipient shall maintain, during the period of implementation of the Operation,the following with staffing and resources appropriate to fulfill their respective functions under the Program and/or theProject:(a) the Coordinating Committee, headed by the Chairman of the TC, to oversee the implementation of the Operation;(b) the Tax Reform Secretariat, headed by the deputy Chairman of the TC, to coordinate tax reform implementation and report tothe Coordinating Committee; and(c) the agencies, offices, units, directorates, working groups within or under MoF and TC and/orunder other relevant ministries, each assigned with technical, social and environmental safeguards, fiduciary and other Program andProject related responsibilities for implementing the Program and the Project, all with functions, capacity, staffing and resourcesappropriate to fulfill their respective functions under the Program and the Project.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section II.A. The Recipient shall ensure that the Program excludes any activities which in theopinion of the Association, are likely to have significant adverse impacts that are sensitive, diverse, or unprecedented on theenvironment and/or affected people.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section II.B. The Recipient shall ensure that the Program excludes any activities which involvethe procurement of: (1) works estimated to cost three million Dollars ($3,000,000) equivalent or more per contract; (2) goods,estimated to cost nine million three hundred seventy five thousand ($9,375,000) equivalent or more per contract; or (3) consultingservices, estimated to cost three million Dollars ($3,000,000) equivalent or more per contract.

baseline.value: Audits are not risk-based. Risk-based selection methodology is developed, but not consistent with international approaches.

target.value: At least 90% of field audits of large taxpayers (i.e. taxpayers with annual turnover above 25 million Somoni) during the Government financial year are conducted for cases selected by the risk-based selection tool.

actual.value: The Bank provided in-person and remote support to ensure completion of the risk analysis matrix and meet DLR 4.2. The TC added and adjusted the risk weight to various indicators leading to the adoption of a risk based framework. As of November 2024, all audit cases are selected through the risk based mechanism

title.narrative: 2.7 Taxpayer Service Standards have been enhanced and based on taxpayer feedback

baseline.value: Quality of taxpayer service is regulated by a Unified Standard for Taxpayer Service (the Standard), enacted in 2017. Implementation of the Standard is not monitored. There is no system for monitoring and continuously enhancing taxpayer services.

target.value: Taxpayer feedback mechanism is established and functional in the Taxpayer Contact Center. Taxpayer feedback mechanism is functional in the Taxpayer Contact Center. Annual reports on taxpayer feedback, collected through the taxpayer feedback mechanism, are publishd at TC website. A Unified Standard for Taxpayer Service is revised based on taxpayer feedback.

actual.value:
The new version of the Unified Taxpayer Service Standards was developed in 2022 on the basis of the Tax Code, which was adopted taking into account proposals from both international financial institutions and feedback from the private sector. Monitoring of the implementation of the Unified Standards is monitored by the relevant Department of the TC and its results are published in the weekly newspaper, and also posted on the official website.
In May, 2024, the TC published a revised unified standards for taxpayer services (meeting DLR 6.3) and registered important progress on the publication of an updated (year 2) annual reports on taxpayer feedback (DLR 6.2). Note that DLR 6.2 year 1 target was achieved. Year 2 target is expected

title.narrative: 3.4 Percentage of VAT refunds processed using risk-based verification or fast track procedures between October 1, 2023 â€“ September 30, 2026.

baseline.value: Risk criteria or fast track procedure are not used for verification of VAT refund.

target.value: 95 % of VAT refunds out of all VAT refunds during the Government financial year are processed using risk-based verification or fast track procedures.

actual.value: 55% of VAT refund claims are processed using the risk-based framework as of Nov 2024

title.narrative: 1.3 Rules for tax and financial accounting reporting for CPT and VAT are harmonized

baseline.value: Rules for establishing a tax base in tax and financial accounting reporting for CPT and VAT are not harmonized.

target.value: New harmonized rules for establishing a tax base in tax and financial accounting reporting for CPT and VAT are enforced.

actual.value: The Decree of the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan on calculating the cost of products, goods, works and services dated October 28, 2023 was approved. The procurement for a new accounting system is underway and expected by December 2024

baseline.value: Tax expenditure report is not prepared and published with the annual draft budget that is submitted to Parliament. Cost-benefit analysis of selected tax incentives/ exemptions is not conducted.

target.value: Tax expenditure report is published with the annual draft budget that is submitted to Parliament. Cost-benefit analysis of selected four tax incentives/ exemptions is conducted and published with the draft annual republican budget.

actual.value: The tax expenditure report was published and a cost benefit analysis of two tax incentives was conducted. The associated DLR 3.1 and 3.2 (year 1) were thus achieved. The TC is now working on meeting year 2 targets. This is expected by February 2025 following the adoption of the new fiscal budget

title.narrative: 3.2 Coverage of corporate taxpayers with annual turnover above 25 million Somoni by Tax Monitoring Program

baseline.value: Tax monitoring is not conducted.There are 242 corporate taxpayers with annual turnover above 25 million Somoni as of September 1, 2020.

target.value: Tax Monitoring Program is fully operational and covers 10 percent of legal entities out of all registered corporate taxpayers with annual turnover above 25 million Somoni.

title.narrative: 2.1 Development and Implementation of a Modern ICT Governance Model

baseline.value: The ICT department does not have an ICT governance model or ICT infrastructure upgrade plan.

target.value: The ICT department operates based on a modern ICT governance model with up to date infrastructure.

actual.value: A new ICT governance model has been developed and approved by the internal regulation.A plan for the implementation of the development of an automated tax administration system for 2020-2025 within the framework of the Project has been developed. According to the ICT Department of the Tax Committee, the process continues and a plan activities has been developed. As of Nov 2024, key achievements include the initial implementation of internal KPIs and further improvements in the software development process, and user feedback system

title.narrative: 1.1 Regulatory foundations for improvement of the tax system established

baseline.value: The new edition of the Tax Code is developed and consulted but not approved. There are no secondary regulations in place to support implementation of the new Tax Code.

target.value: The Recipient has drafted, approved and published on one of the official web-sites the secondary regulations required under the new Tax Code.

actual.value: Following official instructions for MoF, TC and other relevant ministries and agencies to develop and approve the required secondary regulations under the new Tax Code, 86 secondary regulations (ie bylaws) have been issued and officially approved as of Nov 15, 2024

title.narrative: 1.5 Improved representation of women in management positions in TC workforce

baseline.value: Women in managerial positions out of all staff in TC managerial positions comprise 7.8 percent only.

target.value: Women in managerial positions out of all staff in TC managerial positions comprise 11.00 percent.

actual.value: As of Nov 2024, women in managerial positions out of all staff in TC managerial positions surpassed 11%, thereby achieving the associated DLR 7.2 .

title.narrative: (c) Taxpayer satisfaction with the quality of selected new taxpayer electronic services
(a) Taxpayer satisfaction with the quality of selected available taxpayer electronic services
Selected preferential tax and customs incentives eliminated

baseline.value: A new edition of the Tax Code is developed and adopted. The amendments to the Tax Code propose to eliminate at least 14 incentives, related to two preferential tax regimes.

target.value: Tax incentives eliminated under each of the following preferential tax regimes for the new taxpayers:(a) Construction of hydro power plants (for the investor, general contractor and suppliers) (10 incentives); (b) Supply of manufactured products by the investor implementing a production sharing agreement (4 incentives).

actual.value: The new Tax Code of the Republic of Tajikistan (which was approved by the Government on September 2, 2021 and ratified and finally endorsed with Resolution No. 217 of Majlisi Milli of Majlisi Oli of the Republic of Tajikistan on December 17, 2021) eliminated the incentives associated with the construction of hydroelectric power plants (Chapter 46) and persons benefitting from the right to apply for incentives in the implementation of production sharing agreements (Chapter 48), which provided for exemption from payment of 14 taxes and duties.
